title: The Singer is a beautiful story and will teach you a little BSL! ⭐️⭐️...
transcript: The singer is a beautiful new musical with music by Katy Tunstall that tells the story of two different singers, one a deaf man who signs as he performs and the other a hearing individual who sings in a more traditional manner. The two of them meet and write and sing songs together and create this beautiful friendship through their art. The singer is an incredibly moving piece of art, but is also the second show that I've seen this year that is told in both English and sign language. This time in British Sign Language, which is incredibly different from American Sign Language. The singer is also incredibly accessible with the entire show being open captioned and, and primarily signed, which again makes me ask the question, why aren't more shows open captioned? It literally helps everyone. Accessibility is not just for those who need it. The singer can handle performances from four performers. I was in railed by each and every one of them. I thought this show was so incredibly beautiful. And it's one of the shows this year that was under 90 minutes that I wish there was more of. And this didn't feel incomplete at all. I just can see a version of this where we get to sit with these characters and their relationships a little longer. I would love to see this again down the line in a longer format. Give me the two act version of the singer. This was absolutely a Must see for me at the fringe and definitely check it out if you can. The singer is playing through the rest of the fringe at Traverse.
